value: bimodal (most active individuals late morning and afternoon)
method: hourly frequency of active lizards from the recorded time of capture of free-living lizards caught by hand or noose between 10:00 and 19:00 h (no separate activity survey described); Pearson chi-square on hourly frequencies with multiple comparisons (Table IV)
conditions: Free-living lizards at Quebrada Vallecito (Calingasta Department, San Juan Province, Argentina; type locality of the species), captured in October 2008, December 2008 and April 2009; the paper does not say whether the three months were pooled for the hourly pattern (the contingency table combines frequencies per population and activity period). 84 P. williamsi were captured at the site (27 males, 40 females, 17 juveniles); the n used in the hourly analysis is not stated in the text read (Table IV, read only to 13:00, gives 0, 14 and 25 for 10:00-11:00, 11:00-12:00 and 12:00-13:00 h). Activity was inferred from the times lizards were caught active, not from continuous observation, and sampling ran only 10:00-19:00 h (no night or early-morning sampling). Lizards were not released: 'All individuals were collected' under permit, and after the laboratory experiments 'the captured specimens were euthanized' and deposited in a collection; the activity times are field capture times, so not a captive record. The same paragraph reports activity over 7 hours (11:00-18:00 h) with fewer lizards than expected at 13:00-14:00 h (chi-square 13.06, df 21; multiple comparison z = -3.61, P < 0.0001), inside the 'late morning (12:00-14:00 h)' window of the quoted sentence; the syntopic Liolaemus parvus at the same site was unimodal. The paper also measured preferred body temperature in a laboratory gradient, which is not part of this record.
